significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that subliminally acquired misalignment "concentrate[s] along the same single linear 'misalignment direction'" as overt emergent misalignment and that ablating it removes the behavior; this combines a form-(iii) invariance across two induction routes with a form-(ii) causal intervention. It would fix whether the activation feature used for monitoring and steering in OpenAI's 2025 work on a "misalignment persona" also explains the covert transfer reported in Cloud et al.'s Subliminal Learning, thereby determining whether one mechanistic account and control applies to both routes. The claim establishes both a geometric phenomenon and a causal mechanism; its negative branch—"covert channels require their own detection and mitigation"—also discriminates a substantively different account, and the branches are conceptually distinct despite "projects strongly" and "preserving capabilities" lacking quantitative bounds. In the topic-substitution check, merely proposing to extend subliminal learning would not earn this score: the extra weight comes specifically from the pre-identified-direction invariance and its causal reuse across overt and subliminal misalignment.

reach.justification: The named handles are "projection magnitude onto d_mis" as an auditing diagnostic and "direction-ablation defenses" as an intervention. Although the projection is measured after subliminal fine-tuning, both handles can operate before deployment or harmful outputs, giving auditors of distillation pipelines an action window to gate or remediate a student rather than merely explain a failure afterward. After per-model re-extraction, the conclusion predicts a transferable relation—that a model's independently identified emergent-misalignment direction will forecast the later subliminal activation shift—rather than supplying only an open-ended search procedure, though the asserted scope does not clearly cover multiple architectures or misalignment flavors. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: subliminal learning alone supplies neither this pre-deployment diagnostic nor the shared direction-ablation rule, so the reach comes from claim-specific handles rather than the topic's general safety relevance.
